findings.title: Constructor never rejects a null raw token id
findings.body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted, and encodeTokenId concatenates it into a jti ending in ":null". Those token ids are not unique and cannot be correlated with the generated id, while a genuinely null grantType is the only case that throws.

findings.title: Access-token id matcher rejects the expected grant and checks the wrong characters
findings.body: isAccessTokenId returns false when items[0].substring(3, 5) equals the expected grant shortcut, and that slice is not the grant shortcut anyway. The encoded prefix is session(0-1) + token type(2-3) + grant(4-5), so grant must be substring(4, 6), and a match must succeed rather than fail. As written, expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken accept any 6-char prefix plus a UUID and never verify the grant that was just added to the jti, so a wrong or missing grant encoding will not fail those tests.

findings.title: New getShortcut() has no default and is invoked for every grant at startup
findings.body: getShortcut() was added as an abstract SPI method. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit enumerates every OAuth2GrantTypeFactory and calls it. A custom grant factory compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError during provider postInit, which fails Keycloak startup rather than only disabling that grant. A default that yields the unknown shortcut (and is null-safe) is required for compatibility.

findings.title: Shortcut contract says 3 letters but the encoder requires exactly 2
findings.body: The new getShortcut() javadoc tells implementors to return a usually 3-letter shortcut. Decoding in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the context prefix to be exactly 6 characters (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise, and neither postInit nor encodeTokenId checks shortcut length. A grant that follows the javadoc will mint access-token ids that cannot be decoded, so later introspection/session lookup using this context will fail for those tokens.

findings.title: Malformed jti with a colon throws instead of degrading
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId treats a missing colon as a legacy id and returns UNKNOWN, but any id that contains a colon whose prefix is not exactly 6 known shortcuts throws IllegalArgumentException (and the exception text includes the raw token id). Callers that will use this on tokens presented to introspection, userinfo, or admin APIs must catch that or a non-conforming, legacy, or custom jti becomes a 500 instead of the same unknown-context fallback.
